newsitem.title: UK: British attitudes move in favour of abortion - poll.
newsitem.headline: British attitudes move in favour of abortion - poll.

text.p: Thirty years after Britain passed a law permitting doctors to give abortions, poll results out on Thursday showed two out of three people believe women should be allowed to choose whether to terminate their pregnancies.
The MORI poll found a 10 percent swing in support of "legal abortion for all who want it" over the last 17 years, with 64 percent of men and women in favour and 25 percent against.

Sir David Steel, the former Social Democratic Party leader who introduced the 1967 abortion bill, called the results "very comforting". He called for Britain to follow the example of other European countries which allow women to choose abortion up until the 12th or 13th week of pregnancy.
"The fact is public opinion in this country does support the abortion law even if they don't personally approve of abortion," Steel told a news conference.
